title: Cost Management Anomaly Detection

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:cost` events with `matching activity` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.35 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:cost` traffic without `matching activity`. Confirm UC-4.2.35 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:cost` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Cost Management export; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:cost"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.35_cost_management_anomaly_35"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.35 — Cost Management Anomaly Detection: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:cost` for configured audit predicates and returns actor, resource, and region context for cost review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, cost anomalies and waste patterns for 'Cost Management Anomaly Detection' erode FinOps guardrails and often reveal compromised accounts mining resources or forgotten idle infrastructure. UC-4.2.35 drives medium-priority cost alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Ingest daily actual cost by service and resource group. Use `predict` or manual z-score as shown. Alert finance and owners on anomalies. Exclude known one-time purchases via lookup.
visualization: Line chart (daily cost by service), Table (service, z-score), Single value (anomaly count).
knownFalsePositives: Cloud billing and cost files often arrive a day or more late, include credits and refunds, and use tags that do not line up with app names, so a spike is not always a real overrun. We narrow alerts to sustained trends and we exclude test or sandbox projects when we can.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Cost Management export with the modular input for `mscs:azure:cost`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest daily actual cost by service and resource group. Use `predict` or manual z-score as shown. Alert finance and owners on anomalies. Exclude known one-time purchases via lookup.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:cost" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:cost"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.35_cost_management_anomaly_35"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:cost` in `index=azure` to detect cost management anomaly detection. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_35_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (daily cost by service), Table (service, z-score), Single value (anomaly count)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Cost Management export and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cost management anomaly detection so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
